items.text: Among inpatients experiencing homelessness referred from the hospital to housing first in 2024 and 2025, what proportion were housed within six months, what factors were associated with being housed, and how did emergency department visits in the following year compare with matched eligible inpatients who were not referred?
items.population: Inpatients experiencing homelessness at a 480-bed hospital, 2024 and 2025
items.intervention: Referral to housing first by hospital social work (exposure)
items.comparator: Eligible inpatients not referred, matched on prior service use
items.outcome: Housed within six months (referred patients); emergency department visits in 12 months (both groups)
items.time: Six and twelve months after index discharge
items.setting: Inner-city hospital and city housing-first programme

items.text: How do people who were referred, social workers and housing-first staff describe what helps or blocks a hospital referral and what happens in the first weeks after discharge?
items.population: People referred from the hospital, hospital social workers and housing-first staff
items.intervention: Hospital referral to housing first (phenomenon of interest)
items.outcome: Barriers and facilitators to completed referral and early tenancy

finer: Feasible with existing staff, a peer researcher and hospital data, once tenancy data can be shared; interesting to the executive and the provider; novel for this hospital; ethical under the approved outline with conditions; relevant to a pathway decision in 2027.
summary: One PECO question for the quantitative strand and one SPIDER question for the qualitative strand.
